messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ramos <elena@acme-retail.com>, Paul Jenkins <p.jenkins@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Model fit & next steps from today's discovery

Hi Elena / Paul —

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap + next steps from our discovery call so we have a single source of truth: 

Summary of needs:
- Use case: customer support triage + short-form answer generation for product pages (mixed retrieval + generative).
- Traffic profile: expected bursty peak ~120 req/s (TPS) during promotions, baseline ~15–20 TPS.
- Latency target: P95 < 300ms for short responses, P99 < 700ms ideally.
- Quality constraints: prioritize factuality and relevance over creative outputs; hallucination tolerance low.
- Data sensitivity: PHI not present, but PII present — would need VPC + KMS for production.

Recommended immediate next steps:
1) Short eval (2 weeks): run benchmark tests using three model configurations (see attached/links). We suggest Redwood-13B-v2-q4 (low-cost, good latency), Redwood-45B-v1 (higher-quality, higher cost), and a trimmed 34B opt-type we can run in 8k context for retrieval-augmented generation.
2) We'll share benchmark links (TPS, latency percentiles, token cost) and a prompt set for your team to sanity-check outputs.
3) Provide a small sample of anonymized queries (100–200) so we can run ACME-specific evals.
4) Quick follow-up: schedule a 30-min sync next Wed to review results and discuss canary rollout plan.

Attachments: acme_benchmark_summary.pdf (high-level perf), acme_prompt_set_v2.csv (sample prompts), redwood_performance_profiles.csv (model TPS/latency). Links below as well.

If that looks good, I'll kick off the benchmark run and loop in Marissa for the technical details.

Thanks,
Alex

alex.martinez@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0199

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ramos <elena@acme-retail.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 13:05:30 -0700
Subject: Re: Model fit & benchmark links — technical details and profiles

Hi Elena — looping in the technical specifics so you're not relying on product descriptors alone. Short answers below and links to the Redwood-verified performance profiles: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/acme-20260629 (public link for the run we discussed).

Latency & measurement context:
- Payload used for internal tests: ~350 tokens in (prompt + retrieved context) with ~150 tokens expected out. All numbers below are measured under realistic batching (batch size 8) and simulated burst traffic to match ~120 TPS peaks.
- Redwood-13B-v2-q4: P50=42ms, P95=210ms, P99=420ms (single-shard, optimized kernels). TPS sustaining ~180 with our 1-GPU config for short responses.
- Redwood-45B-v1: P50=88ms, P95=360ms, P99=640ms (multi-shard; higher memory + slightly higher variance under bursts). TPS sustaining ~60 in a standard dedicated pool.
- Open-34B-8k (community trim): P50=76ms, P95=330ms, P99=590ms; good trade-off when using retrieval and longer contexts.

Quality / regression note:
- We ran the ACME prompt set (attached acme_prompt_set_v2.csv) through each model and surfaced the top failure modes in the attached acme_benchmark_summary.pdf. The main regression risk we saw is factuality on SKU edge-cases for the 13B quantized variant — acceptable for routing and triage, but for final answer generation we recommend Redwood-45B-v1 or enabling post-retrieval grounding with a stricter reranker.

Redwood verification + profiles:
- "Redwood-XX" models are Redwood-curated and include a verified performance profile (see attached redwood_performance_profiles.csv) with kernel/quantization settings and recommended autoscaling knobs. Community models are denoted in the report and have a "community" tag.

Next steps (technical):
1) If ACME is fine with the trade-offs, we'll provision a dedicated eval pool (VPC) for the 2-week run and seed with your sample queries. That gives exact numbers under your real traffic distribution.
2) We'll export a Prometheus dashboard and share a per-route P95/P99 TTL trace to validate SLAs during the run.
3) If you want lower P99, we can enable prefix KV caching for repeated product descriptions which drops P99 by ~120ms in our simulations.

Attachments are included in this thread. Happy to jump on a screen share Wed morning PT and walk through the dashboard.

—Marissa
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Perfect — thanks for the quick responses and for pulling the queries, Elena. Per Marissa's notes, here are the concrete next steps I'm executing today: 

1) I'll provision the eval pool (restricted VPC) and kick off three parallel benchmark runs against your sample dataset once you share it (please drop to the Drive link or reply-all with the file).
2) Marissa will enable KV prefix caching and export the initial dashboard; we'll send you a link to the live Prometheus view and the perf summary PDF within 24 hours of run start.
3) Proposed canary plan: 1 week of eval traffic in the dedicated pool + targeted A/B tests on 5% of live traffic (if you want to accelerate).

Can we lock Wed 7/1 at 09:30 AM PT for a 30-min sync? I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks — will update you when the runs are started.

Alex
